blocks.text: DynamicPPL runs the probabilistic models used by Turing. A model combines observations with unknown values it generates. Observations contribute a likelihood score. A fixed value is supplied without adding a score.
Previously, conditioning or removing an observation could leave the original model argument in use. This PR stores supplied values and their roles in a binding table on the model.

For readings [1.0, 2.0], condition can replace the second reading with 3.0. decondition can instead make that reading unknown. Both changes leave the original input intact. The next page shows the same calls on both revisions.

blocks.text: Here y holds two readings and mu is their unknown mean. A statement such as y[i] ~ Normal(mu, 1) gives one reading a probability distribution. Calling the model draws unknown values from their priors. It does not fit a posterior.

blocks.title: Two readings
blocks.code:
using DynamicPPL, Distributions, Random

@model function readings(y)
    mu ~ Normal()
    for i in eachindex(y)
        y[i] ~ Normal(mu, 1)
    end
    return y
end
m = readings([1.0, 2.0])
changed = condition(m; y=[1.0, 3.0])
partial = decondition(m, @varname(y[2]))
changed(Xoshiro(1))
partial(Xoshiro(1))

blocks.before: condition(m; y=[1.0, 3.0]) returns [1.0, 2.0]. At mu=0.0 its log likelihood is -4.337877066409345. The model uses the original argument.
blocks.after: The same call returns [1.0, 3.0]. Its log likelihood is -6.837877066409346. The model-owned binding overrides the argument.

blocks.after: The same call returns [1.0, 0.46089361482929836] with Xoshiro(1). The second element is latent. Calling the original m still returns [1.0, 2.0].

blocks.title: Binding and removal rules
rows: A partial binding such as y[2] => 3.0
Supply storage at binding time: a concrete argument, whole binding, storage-carrying VarNamedTuple or final @of template. A later allocation in the body is too late.
A missing or nothing argument
Bind it completely or pass concrete array storage. Templates alone cannot leave part of that argument unbound.
Missing data
Whole missing/nothing arguments and missing elements of a top-level Array can be latent. Nested missing values and placeholders in explicit bindings throw. One multivariate tilde cannot mix roles.
Overlapping observed and fixed values
Remove the old role before assigning the new one. A later binding in the same role replaces selected values.
Dict binding inputs or implicit @vnt import
Use supported named inputs or pairs. InitFromParams still accepts dictionaries. Import @vnt explicitly.
decondition or unfix
Removal reaches submodels too. Removing a whole name covers descendants. Removing an index preserves siblings and does not restore overwritten data.

blocks.title: Submodels and storage
rows: Submodels
Give each child a name. Observe it through condition rather than its arguments. Update addresses to include the child name. Unprefixed submodels are removed.
Partial edits

Supported: Array, array-backed ComponentArray, same-type tuples, SVector, bits MVector, NamedTuple fields and opted-in structs. Unsupported wrappers such as OffsetArray and DimArray require whole-value binding.
Typed storage
Values must fit the declared type exactly. Use runtime-compatible storage for AD values. Remove both roles before changing a root shape.
Prefixes and fields
Use absolute names on prefixed models. Address NamedTuple fields with properties such as y.a.

blocks.current:
Replaces #1523 and #1521. #1502–#1504 will follow as a new series on this PR.

Conditioning and fixing move out of `CondFixContext` into a binding table that each `Model` owns. `conditioned` and `fixed` read it, and `==` and `hash` include it. An argument on a tilde's left-hand side is observed, except where it is wholly `missing` or `nothing`, or at `missing` elements of a top-level `Array`; those are latent and drawn into a copy, so `args` is never mutated. Nested `missing` throws; `main` treated it as latent.

A partial binding such as `x[1] => v` needs storage for `x` at binding time: an argument, a whole binding, a `VarNamedTuple` or an `@of` template. Partial bindings and latent copies support `Array`, array-backed `ComponentArray`, same-type tuples, `SVector`, bits `MVector`, `NamedTuple`, and structs that opt in through `DynamicPPL._binding_optic`. Partial edits of other containers, such as `OffsetArray` and `DimArray`, throw; whole values still bind. Submodels must be named and are observed through `condition`, not their arguments.

Dictionaries are rejected, except by `InitFromParams`. Two changes are silent: argument bindings apply before the body runs, so `ismissing(x)` in `fix(f(missing); x=0.0)` now returns `false`; and `contextualize(new, old.context)` no longer carries bindings. `HISTORY.md` and `docs/src/conditionfix.md` give the migration. Locally, Turing needed small changes; its tests then pass, apart from failures also seen against `main`.

#1523 implements the same design in +4,511 net source lines and +14,799 test lines; this PR needs +1,441 and +2,260. It also fixes three defects in #1523: a binding silently dropped under a prefixed submodel, typed-template constraints never released, and a `MethodError` for a wholly missing slice.
